newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 19.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 19.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Investment bank Morgan Stanley on Tuesday gave Indian corporate debt a "buy" rating and said it was issuing a "message of confidence" in the South Asian nation's economy.

Morgan Stanley said in a statement released in New Delhi that a recent assessment by U.S. credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service Inc, which had called India's creditworthiness unfavourable, was unduly harsh.

Earlier this month Moody's said India's unstable political environment, directionless economic policies and a deterioration in its macroeconomic balances had led it to take an unfavourable outlook on the nation's sovereign rating.
** Securities and Exchange Board of India clears $400 million foreign portfolio investments in debt instruments, says its chief D.R. Mehta
STOCKS TO WATCH:

** The government has told the State Bank of India that the bank would have to stick to the cap of 20 percent fixed for foreign institutional holdings (FII) in public sector banks, the Business Standard reports.
This means that SBI cannot avail of the recent hike in
FII holdings in individual companies to 30 percent from 24 percent, the paper says.
** The boards of Zee Telefilms Zee.BO and Infosys Corporation are thinking of raising the investment ceiling for FII's in their companies to 30 percent, the Economic Times reports.

** The Housing Development Finance Corporation has proposed to move a special resolution at its annual general meeting to allow FII's to increase their holding in the company to 30 percent, the paper says. FII's have already hit the 24 percent ceiling in these firms.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.8750/8850 on Tuesday, dealers said. Tuesday's range is seen at 35.86/89 rupees to a dollar.
The market looks to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), whose dollar buying has been the key factor influencing the market.
** The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange lost 2.95 points, or 0.08 percent, to end at 3,795.17.
** The National Stock Exchange index fell 8.25 points to 1,064.35.
** The Delhi share index added 1.50 points to 788.43.
** The Madras share index gained 12.19 points to 3,602.55.
** The Calcutta index was up 3.94 points to 463.20.
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Smithkline Beecham Consumer on Tuesday said it would offer shareholders three bonus shares for every five held. The stock gained nearly ten percent to close at 296.75 at the Bombay exchange.
